The Nassau Family Court is a specialized court that handles a wide range of family-related legal issues. What is Nassau Family Court?

The Nassau Family Court is a division of the New York State Unified Court System and is responsible for handling a variety of family-related legal issues. These include child custody and visitation, child support, divorce and separation, domestic violence, and adoption, among others. The court is located in Nassau County, New York, and has jurisdiction over cases originating in that county.

History of Nassau Family Court

The evolution of family courts in New York dates back to the late 19th century, when the first family court was established in the state. Over time, the number of family courts in New York expanded, and the Nassau Family Court was established to serve the residents of Nassau County.

The judges of the Nassau Family Court are appointed by the governor of New York and are responsible for handling a variety of family-related legal issues. To be eligible for appointment as a family court judge, an individual must be a resident of New York, a member of the state bar, and have at least 10 years of experience practicing law. Court Procedures in Nassau Family Court

The court procedures in Nassau Family Court are designed to ensure that all parties involved in a case receive a fair and impartial hearing. To file a case in Nassau Family Court, an individual must first complete and file the appropriate legal forms with the court. The next step is to attend a court hearing, where the judge will hear arguments from both sides and make a decision. Representation in Nassau Family Court is not required, but it is highly recommended, as navigating the court system can be complex and challenging without legal assistance.

Types of Cases Handled by Nassau Family Court

Nassau Family Court handles a wide range of family-related legal issues, including child custody and visitation, child support, divorce and separation, domestic violence, and adoption, among others. In child custody and visitation cases, the court determines the legal and physical custody arrangements for children, as well as the terms of visitation. In child support cases, the court determines the amount of support to be paid by one parent to the other to support the children. In divorce and separation cases, the court determines the terms of the divorce, including property division, alimony, and child custody. In domestic violence cases, the court provides protection to victims of domestic abuse through the issuance of restraining orders. In adoption cases, the court finalizes the adoption process and makes the adoption legally binding.

Mediation in Nassau Family Court

Mediation is a process in which a neutral third party helps the parties in a case reach a mutually acceptable resolution. In Nassau Family Court, mediation is often used in child custody and visitation cases, as well as other family-related legal issues, to help the parties avoid a lengthy and costly court battle. The advantages of mediation in family court cases include faster resolution of the case, greater control over the outcome, and lower cost. The mediation process in Nassau Family Court typically involves a series of meetings between the parties and the mediator, during which the parties work together to reach a resolution.

Attorneys also help clients navigate the court system and understand their rights and obligations under the law. In many cases, having a skilled attorney can make a significant difference in the outcome of a case.
